exercises.title: Slow copy
exercises.steps: Copy five letters slowly from a model. Check each shape before writing the next.
exercises.check: Does each letter look like the model?

exercises.title: Letter families
exercises.steps: Write the round family c a d g q o in one row, starting each one the same way.
exercises.example: c a d g q o
exercises.check: Do all round letters start at the same point?

exercises.title: Trace, then write
exercises.steps: Trace a word once, then write it twice on your own without looking.
exercises.check: Is your own copy as clear as the traced one?

tips.text: Start most letters at the top, so every copy of a letter is built the same way.
Slow down for one line: neat shapes come first, speed comes later.

exercises.title: Say the strokes
exercises.steps: Say each stroke out loud as you write it: down, up and round.
exercises.check: Did you start each letter at the top?

exercises.title: Start dots
exercises.steps: Put a small dot where each letter starts, then write the row starting on the dots.
exercises.check: Did every letter begin on its dot?

tips.text: Pull strokes down rather than pushing them up; it is easier to control.
Use the same start point for a letter every time, even in a hurry.

exercises.title: Close the circle
exercises.steps: Write a row of o and a. Join the end of each round back to its start.
exercises.example: o a o a o a
exercises.check: Is every round letter closed, with no gap?

exercises.title: Gap hunt
exercises.steps: Write one sentence, then look for open a, d, g and o. Rewrite any word with a gap.
exercises.check: Could an a be read as a u?

exercises.title: Tall loops
exercises.steps: In joined writing, write l, b and k with narrow, closed loops.
exercises.example: l b k l b k
exercises.check: Are the loops closed and the same width?

tips.text: Think of each round letter as a door: close it before you walk on.
Go back over the top of a and d before the tail; that closes the gap.

exercises.title: Long smooth lines
exercises.steps: Draw slow straight lines and gentle waves across the page without lifting the pencil.
exercises.check: Are the lines smooth, without wobbles?

exercises.title: Light grip
exercises.steps: Hold the pencil lightly and write l and c slowly. Relax your hand between letters.
exercises.example: l c l c l c
exercises.check: Is each stroke one clean line?

tips.text: If your fingers turn white, the grip is too tight. Loosen it and shake out your hand.
A sharp pencil or a smooth pen gives cleaner lines than a blunt one.

exercises.title: Two-line ladder
exercises.steps: Between two light guide lines, write a o e c n m. Every letter touches both lines.
exercises.example: a o e c n m
exercises.check: Do all small letters touch both lines?

exercises.title: Size twins
exercises.steps: Write moon and came. Make all their small letters the same height.
exercises.check: Are the small letters one height?

exercises.title: Fade the guide
exercises.steps: Write a sentence with guide lines, then the same sentence on plain paper.
exercises.check: Did the size stay even without the lines?

tips.text: Match every small letter to the height of the first x or o on the line.
Keep the paper straight in front of you; letters grow when the hand reaches.

exercises.title: Tall and tails
exercises.steps: Write h, l, g and y. Make h and l tall; let g and y go below the line.
exercises.check: Do tall letters reach up and tails go down?

exercises.title: Three zones
exercises.steps: On four-line paper, write words with tall letters and tails, using all three zones.
exercises.check: Is each part of the letter in its zone?

tips.text: Think of three floors: tall letters visit the top floor, tails visit the basement.
Make tall letters about twice the height of small ones.

exercises.title: Sit on the line
exercises.steps: Write one sentence. Circle any letter that floats or dips, then write that word again.
exercises.check: Does every letter sit on the line?

exercises.title: Underline check
exercises.steps: Write a sentence, then draw a ruler line under it. Look for gaps above the ruler line.
exercises.check: Is there an even gap above the ruler line?

exercises.title: Bold writing line
exercises.steps: Go over the writing line in colour so it is easy to see, then write two lines on it.
exercises.check: Do your words stay on the coloured line?

tips.text: Let the pencil touch the line at the bottom of every small letter.
On plain paper, put a dark lined sheet underneath so the lines show through.

exercises.title: Finger spaces
exercises.steps: Write a short sentence. Put one finger after each word before you start the next.
exercises.check: Are the gaps about one finger wide?

exercises.title: Dot the gaps
exercises.steps: Copy the cat sat on a mat. Put a small dot in each gap: are the dots the same distance apart?
exercises.example: the cat sat on a mat
exercises.check: Are all the gaps the same size?

exercises.title: Spaced copy
exercises.steps: Copy two lines from a book, keeping its word gaps, without using your finger.
exercises.check: Can someone read it at a glance?

tips.text: A finger or the width of a pencil is a good gap for children.
If the gaps are right, you can read the line aloud without stopping.

exercises.title: Room inside words
exercises.steps: Write the word letter. Leave the same small gap between every pair of letters.
exercises.check: Do any letters touch or crowd?

exercises.title: Even letter rows
exercises.steps: Write m i n i m in one row. The gaps inside the word should look the same.
exercises.check: Are the letters evenly spread?

tips.text: Letters inside a word sit close but do not touch.
Look at the gap after each letter as you write the next one.

exercises.title: Start at the margin
exercises.steps: Draw a light left margin. Start three short lines right beside it.
exercises.check: Do all lines start at the margin?

exercises.title: Plan the line end
exercises.steps: Before writing a long word near the right edge, check it fits; if not, start it on the next line.
exercises.check: Did any word squeeze at the right edge?

tips.text: Fold the paper once lengthways and open it; the fold makes a quick margin.
Put a finger at the margin and start each line next to it.

exercises.title: Level sentence
exercises.steps: Write a sentence along a ruled line. Keep it level to the end.
exercises.check: Does the end of the line drift up or down?

exercises.title: Steady paper
exercises.steps: Tilt the paper slightly and hold it with your other hand. Write two lines without moving it.
exercises.check: Are the lines straighter than before?

tips.text: Hold the paper with the other hand and move it up as you go down the page.
Look at the end of the line, not just at the pencil.

exercises.title: Matching tall strokes
exercises.steps: Write l and h in a row. Keep their tall strokes at the same angle.
exercises.example: l h l h l h
exercises.check: Are all the tall strokes parallel?

exercises.title: Line up the starts
exercises.steps: Write three short lines, each starting exactly under the line above.
exercises.check: Do the line starts form a straight edge?

tips.text: Tilt the paper the same way every time you write.
Look at the tall stems of l, d and h: they should look like a fence.

exercises.title: Steady count
exercises.steps: Write one letter on each count of a slow, even beat.
exercises.check: Did the letters stay the same while you kept the beat?

tips.text: Write at a speed where letters still look the same.
Short, regular bursts of writing beat one long rushed one.

exercises.title: Light touch
exercises.steps: Write a row pressing lightly, then a row pressing normally. Keep the lighter one.
exercises.check: Is the line the same darkness all the way?

tips.text: Turn the page over: if you can feel the writing, press more lightly.
A softer pencil needs less pressure.

exercises.title: Joined pairs
exercises.steps: In joined writing, write in, an and un without lifting the pencil.
exercises.check: Did the pencil stay on the paper inside each pair?

tips.text: Know where the next letter starts before you finish this one.
Rest the side of your hand on the table and let the wrist move.

exercises.title: One-lift words
exercises.steps: Write short words lifting the pencil only at the end of each word.
exercises.check: Did you lift only at the end?

tips.text: Think a whole word, then write it in one go.
Pause between strokes with the pencil still on the paper.

exercises.title: Same lean
exercises.steps: Write m, i and n slowly. Keep their lean the same.
exercises.example: m i n m i n
exercises.check: Do all letters lean the same way?

exercises.title: Slant guides
exercises.steps: Draw light slant lines across the row, then write two lines following them.
exercises.check: Do your downstrokes follow the guides?

tips.text: Right-handers usually tilt the paper a little left; left-handers a little right.
Upright or leaning, pick one and keep it.

exercises.title: Read it back
exercises.steps: Write two sentences, then ask someone to read them aloud. Rewrite any word they stopped at.
exercises.check: Could they read every word first time?

exercises.title: Best handwriting
exercises.steps: Write two lines in your slowest, clearest handwriting. Compare them with your normal writing.
exercises.check: Which words became easier to read?

tips.text: If a classmate can read it without asking, it is legible.
Fix the one skill that stopped the reader, not everything at once.

exercises.title: Look-alike pairs
exercises.steps: Write a next to o, then c next to e. Make each pair easy to tell apart.
exercises.check: Could anyone mix up any pair?

exercises.title: n, h, r and u
exercises.steps: Write n h r u in a row. Make h tall, close the top of n, and leave u open at the top.
exercises.check: Is each letter clearly itself?

tips.text: Close the top of a, d, g and q so they do not look like u or c.
Make h and k tall so they cannot be read as n or x.

exercises.title: Clean page
exercises.steps: Write a short paragraph with a margin, even gaps and no crossings-out; cross out with one line if you must.
exercises.check: Does the page look tidy from arm's length?

exercises.title: Best copy
exercises.steps: Copy three lines of your own writing into a neat final copy.
exercises.check: Is the final copy neater than the first?

tips.text: Cross out with one straight line instead of scribbling.
Leave a clear space between paragraphs and around the page edges.

tiers._note: defaults; the server resolves the visitor's plan and returns these numbers with /api/v2/me, so a paid plan can change them without a frontend release

selection: only the report's priority skills get practice; exercises per card = min(band.exercises, tier.exercises_max); tips per card = tier.tips_max; both rotate on re-checks
